what: Squashing a branch by hand onto a base that had since moved risked bringing someone else's already-merged changes into the index. Resetting a branch's history onto whatever a base reference currently points at, instead of the shared point where the branch actually diverged, can silently stage far more than the branch itself ever changed.
rule: A squash always resets to the shared point of divergence, never a base reference that may have moved since, and refuses the moment anything unexpected ends up staged.
fix: Enforcement: a new command resets a branch's index to its own point of divergence from the base and refuses, undoing itself first, whenever the newly staged files include one the branch never touched there; it only stages and prints the file list, never committing on its own. Regression coverage is in `tests/field-lessons-batch-w.test.mjs`.
